findings.text: Independent adversarial review at 807d21b: pass_with_notes, 0 blocking. The highest-risk check (did W4 repeat the W3 fail-open) was behaviorally cleared: in a synthetic unproven WARP repo, both the git pre-push hook and the Codex before-shell hook feed the guard the JSON stdin payload and EXIT 2 (block) unproven, EXIT 0 (allow) once a green commit-bound verdict + a proof manifest for HEAD exist; a non-push command passes through (exit 0); an injection command (rm -rf ...) is blocked with zero side-effect (json.dumps). The empty-stdin env-CMD path reproduced the W3 fail-open, proving the stdin-JSON feed is load-bearing.

Three informational notes, none blocking: (1) the Codex editor-hook format is expressed as config.toml [hooks] before_shell and hooks.json beforeShellExecution - a fast-moving surface where at most one spelling is canonical, but the guaranteed enforcement is the git pre-push hook + CI regardless of the editor-hook format, and the hook reads the command from CODEX_COMMAND/CODEX_SHELL_COMMAND or stdin so it works however Codex delivers it; (2) the drift-check flags MISSING/DIFFERS engine files but not EXTRA files (by design - the wrapper is exactly such extra files - not exploitable to hide engine drift); (3) pack-drift enforcement flows through the selftest unit slot of verify.sh, with check_pack_drift.py a convenience CLI over the same mechanism (real either way).

Operational: faithful engine copy (139 files, real, no symlinks); gate GREEN, selftest 1231/0, no pollution of any gate check (packs/codex/specs + plans carry only TEMPLATE.md so the index is not polluted; the dash/genericity sweep covers docs/+plugin/ not packs/); caps byte-identical; authored wrapper + spec dash-clean. Verified GREEN in a clean detached worktree.
